payload.task_text:
I need a regional sales summary focusing on delivered orders from our data warehouse. Please pull the data and break it down by region.

Create an Excel file called Regional_Sales.xlsx in the workspace with two sheets. The first sheet "Regional Breakdown" should have columns Region, Orders (count of distinct delivered orders), Customers (count of distinct customers with delivered orders), Revenue (total amount rounded to 2 decimals), Avg_Order_Value rounded to 2 decimals, and Revenue_Share_Pct showing each region's share of total revenue rounded to 1 decimal. Sort by Region alphabetically.

The second sheet "Summary" with Metric and Value should include Total_Regions, Total_Revenue rounded to 2 decimals, Total_Orders, Total_Customers, and Top_Region being the region name with highest revenue.

Also please create a Google Sheet spreadsheet titled "Regional Sales Dashboard" with a sheet called "Overview" containing the same Regional Breakdown data so the team can access it online.

Task-Solving Rationable with Sub-task Decomposition:
To solve this task efficiently, complete it directly in the main agent and dispatch no sub-agent. One delivered-order regional aggregate is compact, and the local and cloud workbooks consume one frozen table.

Discover and verify `SALES_DW.PUBLIC.ORDERS` and `SALES_DW.PUBLIC.CUSTOMERS`. Join on `CUSTOMER_ID`, filter exact `o.STATUS='Delivered'`, and issue one grouped query by nonblank `c.REGION` returning `COUNT(DISTINCT o.ORDER_ID)`, `COUNT(DISTINCT c.CUSTOMER_ID)`, raw `SUM(o.TOTAL_AMOUNT)`, and raw `AVG(o.TOTAL_AMOUNT)`. Run one independent delivered-population control query for distinct orders/customers and revenue. Compute `Revenue_Share_Pct=100*region_revenue/total_revenue` from unrounded values, sort regions alphabetically, and freeze the complete table plus `Total_Regions,Total_Revenue,Total_Orders,Total_Customers,Top_Region`; choose Top_Region by raw revenue with alphabetical ties and round only displayed money to two decimals/share to one decimal.

Resolve the runtime workspace dynamically. The main agent is the sole writer of `Regional_Sales.xlsx`: create exact `Regional Breakdown(Region,Orders,Customers,Revenue,Avg_Order_Value,Revenue_Share_Pct)` and `Summary(Metric,Value)` with all five literal metrics, then read both full ranges back.

In native parallel with that local write, call `search_spreadsheets(query="Regional Sales Dashboard", max_results=100)` and locally exact-match names. Reuse exactly one result or call `create_spreadsheet(title="Regional Sales Dashboard")` exactly once if absent; block on duplicate exact titles or an ambiguous create. Ensure exactly one `Overview` sheet with the same six headers and every frozen region row, write one complete rectangle with `update_cells`, then read `get_spreadsheet_info` and `get_sheet_data` back. Reconcile cloud/local rows and all regional sums to the source controls without a Wave.

nodes.text:
Create a local Excel deliverable. All work must stay inside this workspace directory: /workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3/SingleUserTurn-sf-sales-regional-summary/workspace

GOAL
Create an Excel file at exactly:
/workspace/dumps/kimi-code_GLM-5.3/SingleUserTurn-sf-sales-regional-summary/workspace/Regional_Sales.xlsx

The file must contain exactly two worksheets with these exact names (in this order):
1. "Regional Breakdown"
2. "Summary"

MOTIVATION / CONTEXT
This is a regional sales summary of DELIVERED orders pulled from the SALES_DW Snowflake warehouse (orders joined to customers on CUSTOMER_ID, filtered to STATUS = 'Delivered'). The aggregation has already been computed and verified — you do NOT need to query Snowflake. Use the numbers below exactly as given.

SHEET 1 — "Regional Breakdown"
Header row in A1:F1 with these exact column names, then one data row per region, sorted alphabetically by Region:
Region | Orders | Customers | Revenue | Avg_Order_Value | Revenue_Share_Pct

Data rows:
- Asia Pacific | 2946 | 416 | 467815.61 | 158.80 | 21.5
- Europe | 2892 | 409 | 458045.46 | 158.38 | 21.0
- Latin America | 2603 | 368 | 395713.16 | 152.02 | 18.2
- Middle East | 2738 | 393 | 444761.21 | 162.44 | 20.4
- North America | 2854 | 412 | 410814.22 | 143.94 | 18.9

Column meanings (do not add extra columns or rows of commentary):
- Orders = count of distinct delivered orders
- Customers = count of distinct customers with delivered orders
- Revenue = total amount, 2 decimals
- Avg_Order_Value = Revenue / Orders, 2 decimals
- Revenue_Share_Pct = region revenue / total revenue * 100, 1 decimal

Numbers must be stored as numeric values (not text strings). Keep the rounding exactly as shown (e.g. 158.80 stays 158.8 numerically, 21.5 stays 21.5 — do not round-trip them into text). Formatting: make the header row bold.

SHEET 2 — "Summary"
Header row in A1:B1 with exactly:
Metric | Value

Then these five rows in this order:
- Total_Regions | 5
- Total_Revenue | 2177149.66
- Total_Orders | 14033
- Total_Customers | 1998
- Top_Region | Asia Pacific

Total_Regions/Total_Revenue/Total_Orders/Total_Customers must be numeric; Top_Region is the text string "Asia Pacific". Make the header row bold.

CONSTRAINTS
- Only use Excel MCP tools (and filesystem tools if needed) on files inside the workspace directory above. Do not touch anything outside it.
- Do not create any additional sheets, charts, or extra files beyond Regional_Sales.xlsx.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA / DELIVERABLE
Confirm by reading back the file (e.g. get_workbook_metadata plus read_data_from_excel on both sheets) that:
- File exists at the exact path above.
- Sheet names are exactly "Regional Breakdown" and "Summary".
- All 6 columns and 5 data rows on sheet 1 match the data above, sorted alphabetically by Region.
- All 5 metric rows on sheet 2 match, and the values are numeric where required.
Report back: the absolute file path, the sheet names, and a confirmation of the read-back verification.
Build Regional_Sales.xlsx

Create an online Google Sheets deliverable using the Google Sheets MCP tools (mcp__google_sheet__*).

GOAL
Create a new Google Spreadsheet titled exactly "Regional Sales Dashboard" containing a worksheet named exactly "Overview".

MOTIVATION / CONTEXT
This is a regional sales summary of DELIVERED orders pulled from the SALES_DW Snowflake warehouse (orders joined to customers on CUSTOMER_ID, filtered to STATUS = 'Delivered'), so the team can access it online. The aggregation has already been computed and verified — you do NOT need to query Snowflake. Use the numbers below exactly as given.

SHEET "Overview" CONTENT
Row 1 header, then one data row per region. Put the header in A1:F1 with these exact column names:
Region | Orders | Customers | Revenue | Avg_Order_Value | Revenue_Share_Pct

Data rows (in this order, already sorted alphabetically by Region):
- Asia Pacific | 2946 | 416 | 467815.61 | 158.80 | 21.5
- Europe | 2892 | 409 | 458045.46 | 158.38 | 21.0
- Latin America | 2603 | 368 | 395713.16 | 152.02 | 18.2
- Middle East | 2738 | 393 | 444761.21 | 162.44 | 20.4
- North America | 2854 | 412 | 410814.22 | 143.94 | 18.9

Column meanings (do not add extra columns, extra rows, or commentary):
- Orders = count of distinct delivered orders
- Customers = count of distinct customers with delivered orders
- Revenue = total amount, 2 decimals
- Avg_Order_Value = Revenue / Orders, 2 decimals
- Revenue_Share_Pct = region revenue / total revenue * 100, 1 decimal

Write numbers as numeric values, not text strings (e.g. 467815.61, 158.80, 21.5 — not "467815.61").

STEPS / NOTES
- Use mcp__google_sheet__create_spreadsheet with title "Regional Sales Dashboard". Note that a new spreadsheet typically starts with a default tab (often "Sheet1") — you must end up with a tab named exactly "Overview". Either rename the default tab to "Overview" (mcp__google_sheet__rename_sheet) or create a new sheet named "Overview" and make sure no leftover default tab remains (delete it via mcp__google_sheet__batch_update deleteDimension if necessary).
- Do not add any other sheets/tabs.
- Do not share the spreadsheet with anyone and do not send any emails.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA / DELIVERABLE
Verify by reading the data back (mcp__google_sheet__list_sheets and mcp__google_sheet__get_sheet_data on "Overview") that the spreadsheet title, tab name, and all cell values match the data above.
Report back: the spreadsheet ID, its URL (if returned), the spreadsheet title, the list of tab names, and a confirmation of the read-back verification.
